CSCA Preparation: How to Prepare for the CSCA Exam

To prepare for the CSCA, confirm which subjects your program needs, study the official syllabus, use free Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry practice to find gaps, then take full timed mocks for the papers available. Prepare for Professional Chinese with its track syllabus and reading practice if your program requires it.

Try five free questionsCheck the official syllabi
Five questions per subject, with no sign-up needed. Full timed mocks require Full Access.

How to prepare for the CSCA in 6 steps

Follow these steps in order. Each one links to the page that covers it in detail.

Step 1
Confirm which subjects you need

Mathematics is required for every applicant, while Physics and Chemistry depend on the program. Chinese-taught applicants generally take Professional Chinese. Published guidance differs for fully English-taught scholarship applicants, so confirm your exact subjects with your university before planning or registering.

CSCA subjects by major

Step 2
Learn the exam format

Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry each have 48 single-choice questions in 60 minutes, so you get about 75 seconds per question. Professional Chinese has 80 questions in 90 minutes. Every paper is scored from 0 to 100.

CSCA format and scoringWhat is the CSCA exam?

Step 3
Take a free diagnostic test

Start with a short timed practice set for each Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry paper you need. Your mistakes show which topics need work. If you also need Professional Chinese, use its official track syllabus to identify vocabulary and reading gaps; CSCA.ai does not offer a Chinese practice set yet.

Free CSCA practice tests

Step 4
Study topic by topic from the syllabus

Start with the organizer's syllabus PDF for each required subject, then use its sample questions to see the published question style. Learn one syllabus topic at a time, answer independent practice questions, and revisit the types you get wrong each week. Direct PDF links are below.

CSCA syllabusLessons and quizzes

Step 5
Switch to full timed mock tests

In the final weeks, use full 48-question, 60-minute mocks for the Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry papers you need. CSCA.ai offers these mocks through Full Access; the five-question subject sets are free without sign-up. Professional Chinese has 80 questions in 90 minutes, but CSCA.ai does not offer a mock for it yet. Use its official track syllabus and clearly sourced reading practice. Check your session's permitted-materials rules, then review every wrong answer before the next mock.

30 CSCA mock testsHow to use mock tests

Step 6
Register early and plan exam day

The published calendar lists six sittings from November 2026 through June 2027, each with its own registration window. Check csca.cn for the current notice and register before your chosen session closes. Test your device and room a week before a home-based exam.

CSCA exam datesHow to registerExam-day tips

Your first seven days of CSCA preparation

Start with your university’s requirements and the official syllabus, then use a short practice set to find your first gaps. This is an example routine you can adjust to your subjects and exam date.

Day 1

Confirm your papers

Read each target university’s admission notice. Write down the CSCA subjects, test language and application deadline it requires.

Day 2

Mark the official syllabus

Open the organizer’s PDF for every required subject. Mark each topic as familiar, partly known or new; this becomes your study checklist.

Day 3

Take a short baseline

Try the free five-question practice set in each available subject without notes. Record the questions you guessed or missed. A short set is a starting signal, not a full readiness score.

Day 4

Repair one gap

Choose one missed syllabus topic. Read a lesson or worked example, then solve a few similar questions and explain the method in your own words.

Day 5

Review your errors

Redo the questions you missed without looking at the answer. Note whether each error came from a concept gap, a calculation slip, a misread term or time pressure.

Day 6

Practise the next topic

Study another weak topic from your official syllabus and answer a fresh short set. Compare the result with your first attempt.

Day 7

Choose the longer plan

Use your topic checklist and error log to choose a 4-, 8- or 12-week plan below. Schedule topic study, review and full-length mocks where available before your exam date.

This is CSCA.ai study guidance, not an official timetable. The Shanghai government’s CSCA preparation guide recommends checking university subject requirements, using the official syllabus, practising weak areas and keeping an error log. Try a free short practice set to begin.

Keep a CSCA practice error log

After each practice set or mock, record the syllabus topic, your answer, the correct method, why you missed it, and when you will try a similar question again. Review the log each week to choose which topics to study next.

For example, in our own Mathematics practice question about a set with four elements, choosing 16 instead of 15 proper subsets means you counted the whole set. Write “subtract one from 2ⁿ” as the correction, then solve a new subset question without notes the next day. This is a study example, not an official exam question.
Download the blank CSCA error log (CSV)
Open the file in a spreadsheet app. It contains column headings only; your entries stay on your device unless you choose to share them.

How long should you prepare for the CSCA?

Use the 4-, 8- or 12-week example plan that fits your starting point and time before the exam, then adjust it after your diagnostic test. For a day-by-day version, see the 90-day CSCA study plan.

12 weeks

Best for: Starting from scratch, or taking three subjects

Weeks 1–2: diagnostic test, then fill gaps in the topics you got wrong

Weeks 3–8: one syllabus topic at a time, with practice questions after each

Weeks 9–11: one timed mock each week for each required Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry paper; review mistakes and keep practising Chinese reading if required

Week 12: light revision of your mistake list and exam-day setup

8 weeks

Best for: Comfortable with the content, need exam practice

Week 1: use available subject sets for a baseline; map Professional Chinese gaps to its syllabus if required

Weeks 2–5: weakest topics first, practising timed question sets

Weeks 6–7: two full mocks a week for each required Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry paper; keep Chinese reading timed if required

Week 8: review explanations and rest before the exam

4 weeks

Best for: Registered for the next sitting

Week 1: use available practice sets and pick three weak topics for each required paper

Weeks 2–3: study those topics and take full mocks where available every few days

Week 4: final available mocks, mistake review and exam-day checklist

Self-study or a CSCA preparation course?

Start with the official syllabus and a short practice set. If you can learn the missed topics independently, keep studying at your own pace. If you need help understanding them or staying on schedule, a teacher-led course may help.

Study on your own

Follow the syllabus, use the free five-question subject practice to identify gaps, and work through lessons and your error log. Full-length timed mocks require Full Access; the short practice sets do not require sign-up.

Official syllabus linksTry free practiceSee timed mocks

Learn with a teacher

CSCA.ai live classes cover Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry in English, with worked examples and time for questions. Choose only the subjects your university requires, then check each batch’s schedule and price before enrolling. Live classes are sold separately from Full Access.
Compare live classes

The Shanghai government preparation guide recommends using the official syllabus and practising weak areas; it suggests online courses when a concept is difficult to learn alone. CSCA.ai classes and practice are independent of the exam organizer.

Which CSCA preparation books and PDFs should you use?

Start with the organizer’s free syllabus PDF for each subject your university requires, then its Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry sample-question PDFs. They show the published topics and example question style. A textbook can help you learn a weak topic, but a “CSCA” label on a book does not make it an official exam resource.

Official syllabus PDFs

Use these as your topic checklist. Choose a book or lesson only for topics that need work. The direct links for all four subjects are in the subject section below.

Open the official syllabi

Official sample PDFs

Use the organizer’s Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry samples to inspect the published question style. A sample is not a complete past paper or a forecast of the next sitting’s questions.

Find sample PDFs and worked examples

Subject textbooks

Choose a high-school-level book in your test language with clear worked solutions for the syllabus topics you need. Compare its exercises with the official samples; third-party books may use a different level or format.

Compare CSCA preparation books and free PDFs

For example, if functions are difficult in Mathematics, find that topic in the official syllabus, study a worked explanation in your textbook, then try an official sample and a different practice question. The Shanghai government’s CSCA guide also recommends making the official syllabus the basis of your review. Checked 10 November 2026.

CSCA preparation by subject

Every paper is scored from 0 to 100, and each university sets the scores it accepts. Prepare for the subjects your program asks for.

How to prepare for CSCA Mathematics

Required for everyone. Covers sets and inequalities, functions and sequences, geometry and algebra, and probability and statistics. Practise working every calculation by hand.

Mathematics syllabusFree Mathematics practiceOfficial Mathematics syllabus PDFOfficial Mathematics sample PDF

How to prepare for CSCA Physics

Usually needed for engineering and science programs. The official syllabus has five modules: Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics, Optics and Modern Physics. Learn the standard formulas until you can apply them quickly.

Physics syllabusFree Physics practiceOfficial Physics syllabus PDFOfficial Physics sample PDF

How to prepare for CSCA Chemistry

Usually needed for medicine, pharmacy and laboratory sciences. Covers core concepts and calculations, properties and reactions, chemical theories and laws, and experiments. Practise balancing equations and mole calculations quickly.

Chemistry syllabusFree Chemistry practiceOfficial Chemistry syllabus PDFOfficial Chemistry sample PDF

How to prepare for CSCA Professional Chinese

Confirm whether your program requires Professional Chinese and which track—Humanities or STEM. The official outlines differ. Fully English-taught scholarship applicants should check their requirement with the university because published guidance differs. The paper has 80 questions in 90 minutes, in Chinese.

Professional Chinese syllabusOfficial Humanities Chinese syllabus PDFOfficial STEM Chinese syllabus PDF

CSCA preparation questions

How do I prepare for the CSCA exam?

Confirm which subjects you need, learn the format, use the available Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry practice sets to find gaps, and study each official syllabus. Finish with full timed mocks for those available papers; use track-specific reading practice for Professional Chinese if required. Register as soon as your session's window opens.

How long does CSCA preparation take?

The time you need depends on your starting point, required subjects and exam date. Use our 4-, 8- or 12-week example plans, then adjust after a short practice set shows your weak topics.

Can I prepare for the CSCA for free?

Yes. CSCA.ai has free practice tests in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry without sign-up, plus free lesson units after you create an account. The official syllabus is published on csca.cn. Full Access unlocks the remaining lessons and full timed mocks; live classes are sold separately.

Which CSCA preparation book should I use?

Start with the organizer's syllabus and sample-question PDFs for each subject your university requires. If you use a textbook, choose one in your test language that explains the syllabus topics you need, then compare its exercises with the official samples. A book's CSCA label does not make it an official exam resource. The official PDF links are in the subject section above.

Are there CSCA past papers?

The organizer publishes sample-question PDFs for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, but these are not verified complete past papers. CSCA.ai's mock tests are independent preparation questions, not official exam papers. Check csca.cn for the latest released material for your session.

Can I use a calculator in the CSCA?

The published subject syllabus does not establish a universal calculator rule. Check the candidate notice and permitted-materials instructions for your session on csca.cn before test day. Working calculations by hand is still useful practice.

Do I need live classes to pass the CSCA?

No, many students prepare on their own with practice questions and mock tests. Live classes help if you want a teacher to explain difficult topics, keep you on a schedule and answer questions as you go.

Source check: 25 October 2026. CSCA.ai is an independent preparation platform. The organizer’s linked PDFs are official syllabi and sample questions; our practice and mocks are independent. Check the official CSCA exam introduction and the current notices on csca.cn for rules, dates and fees.
